title: Vote chori. A claim, an ultimatum, and no audit

Achary has said Rule 20(3)(b) governs claims and objections in the window after a draft roll is published and cannot apply after an election, which would mean the only route the Commission offered does not exist. title: Gujarat 2002. What the courts found, and what they did not

human.v: 1,044 killed on the official count given to Parliament — 790 Muslims and 254 Hindus — with 223 missing, 2,548 injured, 919 women widowed and 606 children orphaned. 59 died in the Godhra train fire that preceded it

cost.v: ₹204.62 cr spent by the state on relief and rehabilitation; ₹1.5 lakh ex gratia for each person killed

what: Fifty-nine people died when coaches of the Sabarmati Express were set alight at Godhra on 27 February 2002. Communal violence followed across Gujarat over the following weeks. The official toll, given to the Rajya Sabha in May 2005, was 1,044 dead.
dodge: In July 2002 the National Human Rights Commission found a 'comprehensive failure on the part of the State Government to control the persistent violation of the rights to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the people of that State', and recommended five cases be transferred to the CBI. The state government declined, and without its request the Centre said the CBI could not take over. The Supreme Court twice found a fair trial impossible in Gujarat and moved cases out of the state: nine of the twenty-one Best Bakery accused were convicted only on retrial in Mumbai, after all had been acquitted at home. Convictions followed at Sardarpura, Ode, Naroda Patiya and Gulberg Society, and many did not survive appeal. In 2024 the Supreme Court quashed Gujarat's remission of the eleven Bilkis Bano convicts, holding the state was not the competent government and had 'acted in tandem and was complicit' with them. Across twenty-four years, no minister resigned.

ministers.r: NHRC found comprehensive failure to control the violence; declined the CBI transfer
Chief Minister; SIT found no prosecutable evidence, upheld by the Supreme Court in 2022

pos: The state's position, substantially accepted by the Supreme Court in June 2022, is that a mob attacked the train at Godhra and that the violence which followed was spontaneous rather than state-sponsored, that the administration moved as fast as an inadequate police force allowed and sought central forces and the Army promptly, and that the then Chief Minister made repeated public appeals for peace. alleg: Zakia Jafri's allegation of a larger conspiracy involving the then Chief Minister and 63 officials was rejected by the SIT in 2012, a magistrate in 2013, the Gujarat High Court in 2017 and the Supreme Court in 2022. Death tolls above the official 1,044 are estimates by rights organisations and are not court-established. Maya Kodnani, convicted in 2012, was acquitted by the Gujarat High Court in 2018.
alt: A state that accepts a national human rights body's recommendation to move investigations out of its own hands, trials that need not be transferred to another state to be fair, and political responsibility that does not wait on a criminal conviction.

title: Fuel excise. The crude crash the consumer never saw

human.v: Every household buying fuel through the pandemic, and every state whose share shrank as the levy moved into cesses it does not receive

cost.v: ₹24.85 lakh cr of central excise from petroleum, 2014-15 to 2023-24. Duty on petrol went from ₹9.48 to ₹32.98 a litre, diesel from ₹3.56 to ₹31.83. Of ₹27.90 on petrol in 2022, only ₹1.40 was shareable with states

what: The government told Parliament it raised excise duty on ten occasions between November 2014 and January 2016 'to take away gains arising from a fall in international oil prices', and again by ₹13 a litre on petrol and ₹16 on diesel between March and May 2020 'when international oil prices came crashing after the onset of the pandemic'. Duty peaked at ₹32.98 on petrol on 6 May 2020. Excise from the petroleum sector jumped from ₹2.23 lakh crore in 2019-20 to ₹3.73 lakh crore in 2020-21.
dodge: Almost none of it is shared. The Finance Minister confirmed in 2022 that of ₹27.90 a litre of central tax on petrol, only ₹1.40 was basic excise duty shareable with states, and that both the November 2021 and May 2022 cuts were made entirely in the non-shareable Road and Infrastructure Cess. The CAG has repeatedly found the cess money is not reaching the funds it was levied for: ₹10,157 crore of Road and Infrastructure Cess in 2018-19 'was neither transferred to the related Reserve Fund nor utilised for the purpose for which the cess was collected', and a separate ₹10,250 crore was moved out by a journal entry after the year closed, which the CAG said was done 'primarily for the purpose of artificially inflating revenue receipts of the year', had 'the effect of understating deficit', put money to purposes 'contrary to the will of the Parliament', and merited investigation of the officials who authorised it. The Ministry's defence was called untenable.

ministers.r: Set duty and cess structure; CAG defence on cess accounting held untenable
Union Finance Minister; confirmed cuts were made in the non-shareable cess

pos: The government's position is that excise is a legitimate policy instrument calibrated as required, that it cut duty by ₹13 a litre on petrol and ₹16 on diesel across November 2021 and May 2022 and passed the relief fully to consumers, that state finances were unaffected because the cuts came from a cess states never received, and that large subsidy outlays must be set against the revenue. On the accounting, it argued the transfer followed the redesignation of the Central Road Fund and had precedent.
alleg: The CAG's language is 'not transferred' and 'short-credited', not diverted or misappropriated. The CAG also notes cess shortfalls date back to levies imposed in 1974 and therefore span multiple governments. Calling the 2020 increases a windfall is fair comment on figures the government itself gave Parliament; calling it profiteering is opinion.
alt: Cess proceeds credited to the funds they were raised for, an honest split between shareable duty and cess, and duty that falls when crude falls.

title: The cylinder. Subsidy withdrawn, refills never came

title: The air. A million dead a year, and a target quietly missed

human.v: 2.1 million deaths in India attributed to air pollution in 2021, including 169,400 children under five. The 2019 figure was 1.67 million, 17.8% of all deaths that year

cost.v: US$36.8 bn lost in 2019, about 1.36% of GDP — roughly ₹2.6 lakh cr in that year alone

what: The National Clean Air Programme set out to cut PM10 by 20 to 30% by 2024-25, then revised the goal to up to 40% by 2025-26. By CREA's January 2026 assessment, only 23 of the 130 cities covered had reached the revised target and most remain above national standards. Delhi was ranked the world's most polluted capital for an eighth consecutive year at 82.2 µg/m³ of PM2.5, more than sixteen times the WHO guideline and above India's own weaker 40 µg/m³ standard.
dodge: The Supreme Court has been unusually blunt. In September 2024 it told the Commission for Air Quality Management that 'like pollution, your directions are in the air' and found total non-compliance with the Act. In November 2024 it held that the right to live in a pollution-free environment is a fundamental right under Article 21, found a serious lapse by the Delhi government and police on enforcement, and directed prosecution under Section 14 of the CAQM Act, which carries up to five years in prison. Complaints followed against 111 officials of Punjab and Haryana. Not one minister, state or Union, has resigned or been removed, and the target year passed without an accounting.

ministers.n: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
ministers.r: Owns NCAP; revised target missed, no accounting published
Statutory powers since 2021; found in total non-compliance by the Supreme Court

pos: The government's position is that air pollution is a diffuse, trans-boundary problem spanning crop residue burning, construction, industry, vehicles and winter meteorology that no single authority controls, which is precisely why it created the CAQM in 2021 as a statutory body with penal powers across four states. It points to city-specific action plans under NCAP, a large expansion of monitoring, and real reductions in a number of cities as evidence that a structural problem is being addressed.

alt: A target with a named owner and a published annual reckoning, enforcement that reaches the people who set policy rather than only district officials, and a national standard that matches the WHO guideline.

title: Cow protection. 44 dead, and a record export year

human.v: At least 44 people killed and around 280 injured in cow-related violence between May 2015 and December 2018, 36 of the dead Muslim, across more than 100 incidents in 20 states. There is no official count after 2017

cost.v: ₹34,392 cr of buffalo meat exported in 2024-25 — 79.4% of India's entire animal-product export basket — while cow slaughter stays banned across most states

More than a decade after Mohammad Akhlaq was killed at Dadri in September 2015 there has been no conviction; all fourteen surviving accused are on bail, and in October 2025 the state applied to withdraw the prosecution entirely, a plea a fast-track court rejected that December. In Rakbar Khan's case four men were convicted in 2023, but of culpable homicide rather than murder, and given seven years. Eleven men convicted for killing Alimuddin Ansari were bailed on appeal in 2019, and a Union minister had already garlanded eight of them at his residence in July 2018, calling it honouring due process. Then the counting stopped: the NCRB gathered data on mob lynching and cow vigilantism for 2017, never published it, and discontinued collection on the ground that the crimes were not defined.

On lynchings it says vigilantism is an ordinary crime for state police to prosecute under existing law, that the Prime Minister has publicly condemned cow vigilantism, and that a Group of Ministers was constituted. On data it maintains the NCRB can only publish under heads defined in statute, and mob lynching was not one.

cost.v: Not a money case. India went from 140th of 180 on the RSF press freedom index in 2014 to 157th in 2026, inside the band RSF calls 'very serious'

title: 2G spectrum. A ₹1.76 lakh crore estimate, and not one conviction
